key_insight: TEON generalizes the Muon optimizer by modeling gradients as a structured higher-order tensor and applying tensorized orthonormalization across modes, yielding stronger convergence guarantees than layer-wise (matrix) orthogonalization.
problem_solved: Layer-wise Muon treats each layer independently and misses cross-layer and multi-mode correlations in gradients; TEON addresses this by removing redundancy and collinearity in a tensor-structured gradient representation to improve optimization for large language model pre-training.
method: Represent the network gradients (or momenta) as a structured higher-order tensor that captures interactions across parameter modes (e.g., layers, heads, channels).
Perform tensorized orthonormalization across tensor modes (mode-wise / multi-mode orthogonalization) to decorrelate gradient components beyond per-layer matrices.
Design scalable approximations and algorithmic steps that retain provable improved convergence over layer-wise Muon while remaining practical for LLM-scale pre-training.
impact: TEON can make LLM pre-training more stable and sample-efficient by removing multi-mode gradient redundancies, enabling faster convergence and more robust scaling of optimizer behavior across very large models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side illustration: matrix (layer-wise) orthonormalization vs tensorized (multi-mode) orthonormalization showing additional cross-mode decorrelation.
Schematic tensor diagram labeling modes (layers, heads, channels) with arrows showing mode-wise orthonormal transforms.
Convergence chart: training loss or validation perplexity curve comparing TEON vs Muon and baseline optimizers (faster drop / lower final loss for TEON).
Algorithm flow diagram: gradient tensor construction → mode-wise orthonormalization → update step, with a callout for scalable/approximate computations.
paper_title: TEON: Tensorized Orthonormalization Beyond Layer-Wise Muon for Large Language Model Pre-Training
paper_authors: Ruijie Zhang, Yequan Zhao, Ziyue Liu, Zhengyang Wang, Dongyang Li
